newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rosneft says to absorb Purneftegaz shares longterm.
newsitem.headline: Rosneft says to absorb Purneftegaz shares longterm.

text.p: Shares of Russian oil production company Purneftegaz PFGS.RTS will be combined with those of holding company Rosneft after the holding is privatised, a Rosneft spokesman said on Thursday.

He said that Rosneft-Purneftegaz 0#PFGS.RUO, as the producer is known, had dropped plans to issue American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), on hold for about two years, because of the plan to combine shares.

"Rosneft must be privatised and issue shares first, then we will look into uniting the shares. It is a long process," said spokesman Vladimir Tumarkin. He said that other Russian holding companies took years to carry out such plans.
"Today it (the ADR plan) is not viable because they are looking at a single share with Rosneft," he said. An ADR would allow Purneft shares to be traded on Western exchanges.

Rosneft owns 38 percent of Purneft and has 51 percent of voting stock. Russia plans to privatise Rosneft this year. Interfax news agency said in February Russia would sell off 48 percent of the company through tenders and auctions.
Purneftegaz produced 8.48 million tonnes of oil (169,600 barrels per day), up from 8.31 million tonnes (166,200 bpd) in 1995.
SIDANKO oil holding company, which briefly held Purneftegaz in 1994, is seeking its return in court, though it has lost a number of cases.
